chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who became junub, then performed tayammum with earth and prayed, then later found water.
So he عليه السلام said: He does not repeat it. Indeed, the Lord of water is the Lord of earth; thus he has performed one of the two purifications.

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ritual purification
key_terms.الصَّعِيدِ: earth or clean ground used for tayammum
key_terms.الطَّهُورَيْنِ: the two valid means of purification, water and earth
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water used for ghusl or purification
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as dry ablution in place of water
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ: he does not repeat the prayer

ai.seo_question: If a junub person prays with tayammum and later finds water, must he repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a junub person who performs tayammum due to the absence of water and then offers salat. If he later finds water, he is not required to repeat the prayer, because tayammum is a valid form of taharah when water is unavailable.
